## Wave 5 Summary

Wave 5 is the NCG / operator-algebra cluster for S97. It does four structurally distinct things, all sourced from S96 carry-forwards. (1) **5.1 `S97-DK-DF-STAGE2`** promotes the W8-4 `D_K≅D_F` *controlled-recovery* theorem through the `joint-theorem-promotion.md` 4-stage pathway: it lands the recovery as a `permanent-results-registry.md §VII.BH` STAGE-1-CANDIDATE (next-free slot, §VII.BG being the highest currently in use), then runs the mandatory two-agent Stage-2 cross-axis independent-verify (Axis-A NCG-axiomatic = connes-ncg-theorist; Axis-B substrate/superfluid = volovik-superfluid-universe-theorist), both WITHOUT prior workshop context, JOINT clauses PASS-AND'd. This is warranted precisely because the recovery is *conditional* — it holds on the algebra-side N7 rescue class (the (0,0)-sector quotient reproducing the SM finite geometry on 4 criteria) while the bare-axiom N3 (order-one failure at norm 4.000) and the product-vs-finite KO-mismatch (fiber wants KO-dim=6; SU(3)-orbital gives 0; product gives 4) remain PERMANENT obstructions. The verdict-state of those obstructions IS a joint clause both reviewers must independently affirm. (2) **5.2 `S97-Q10-1-PS-CONDENSATE`** computes `ker(ι_*^{PS})` on the Pati–Salam extended triple `A_K^{PS}=ℂ⊕M₂(ℂ)_L⊕M₂(ℂ)_R⊕M₄(ℂ)` and decides whether `M₄(ℂ)` admits a non-abelian symmetry-breaking condensate channel, or whether the `A_K` abelian-only / color-singlet-forced theorem EXTENDS to the PS algebra. (3) **5.3 `S97-DS-AREA-LAW-MONOTONICITY`** decides whether the de Sitter / cosmological-horizon area law `S_dS=A/4G_N` admits an INDEPENDENT substrate-spectral-monotonicity derivation (the cosmological analog of the S63 black-hole chain) or merely inherits the BH derivation through the `a₀/a₂` ratio lock. (4) **5.4 `S97-VN-TYPE-INDUCTIVE-LIMIT`** establishes the Murray–von Neumann type of the inductive limit `lim_{L_max→∞}(A_K^{≤L},H_K^{≤L},D_K^{≤L})` — DS.1 proved each finite stage is finite Type-I; this settles whether the tower-completion stays Type-I (expected AF / hyperfinite Type-I_∞) or changes type.

Carry-forward source: S96 W8-4 (5.1, `session-96-w8-workingpaper.md` line 640); S96 NYT-Q10 BdG-vs-Yang-Mills workshop (5.2, `workshops/session-96-NYT-Q10-bdg-gap-vs-yang-mills.md` line 532); S96 NYT-Q7 NCG-dof-vs-M-theory workshop (5.3 = CF-1 line 985; 5.4 = CF-2 line 992).

**Wave-classification (per `.claude/rules/wave-classification.md`)**: Wave 5 is **MIXED-class** and is sub-wave-decomposed at plan-freeze. 5.1 carries TWO components: (i) a METHODOLOGY-class **registry-landing** component (write the §VII.BH STAGE-1-CANDIDATE entry — artifact-existence + content, no numerical threshold) and (ii) a COMPUTE-class **Stage-2 cross-axis verify** component (the two-reviewer PASS-AND has a structured PASS/FAIL/INFO outcome). 5.2 / 5.3 / 5.4 are COMPUTE-class (structural-existence / set-membership / characterization gates with explicit PASS/FAIL/INFO criteria, per the R3 YAML "NON-COMPUTE gate note" — set-membership and characterization gates set the numerical-threshold PRDR items to N/A with a one-word reason and pin the real criterion in `operator` + the verdict rubric). substitution_chain:
```yaml
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "The recovery is a CONTROLLED low-energy quotient (not a full isometric
            isomorphism), and the N3 + product-vs-finite KO-mismatch remain PERMANENT
            obstructions; therefore the registry tag is a CONDITIONAL controlled-recovery

    Step 1 (Definitions, cited from s96_consol_dk_df_equiv.npz):
      crit_i_AF_Wedderburn   = True     [AF-Wedderburn factorization matches A_F = ℂ⊕ℍ⊕M₃(ℂ)]
      crit_ii_KOdim6         = True     [the (0,0)-sector finite triple carries KO-dim 6]

      crit_iv_KKgap          = True     [KK_gap_over_MKK = 0.6822573526 ∈ [KK_GAP_LO, KK_GAP_HI] = [0.5, 2]]

      recovery_residual_literal              = 0.17053605699   [literal residual]
      recovery_residual_KK_suppression_budget = 0.32022701757  [= O((E_low/M_KK_eff)²) budget]
      KO_dim_fiber           = 6        [the FIBER demands KO-dim 6]
      KO_dim_SU3_orbital     = 0        [the SU(3) orbital sector carries KO-dim 0]
      KO_dim_product         = 4        [the product geometry yields KO-dim 4]

    Step 2 (Substitute — what "recovery" means):
      recovery = (quotient by the KK tower at E ≪ M_KK)
               ⇒ retain only the (0,0) const-mode block (96→16 via the const-mode projection;
                 const_mode_abs_evals has 16 entries, C2_const_mode = 0.0)
               ⇒ the 4 criteria all hold on that block (crit_i..crit_iv all True)
               ⇒ the residual is NOT zero (literal_exact = False) but is bounded by the
                 KK-suppression budget (0.320).

    Step 3 (Simplify — controlled vs isomorphism):
      literal_exact = False  ⇒  the map is NOT a bit-for-bit isometric isomorphism.
      But (4 criteria True) ∧ (residual ≤ 0.320 = O((E/M_KK)²))  ⇒  the (0,0) block
        reproduces D_F up to a controlled, parametrically-suppressed error.
      Therefore the correct epistemic type is CONTROLLED RECOVERY, not EQUIVALENCE.

    Step 4 (Direction — obstructions are PERMANENT, read off the KO record + N3):
      KO_dim_product = 4  ≠  KO_dim_fiber = 6   ⇒  the product geometry CANNOT supply the
        KO-dim=6 the finite triple needs from the SU(3)-orbital (which is 0); this is a
        STRUCTURAL mismatch at the bare-axiom level, NOT a low-energy artifact —
        quotienting by the KK tower does NOT change KO_dim_product (it is a property of the
        PRODUCT M₄ × F, fixed independent of E). Hence PERMANENT.
      N3 (order-one failure at norm 4.000, S58): the order-one condition [[D,a],b°]=0 fails
        at the (H,H) entry with value 4.000 on the bare product triple; the controlled
        recovery does NOT repair N3 (it only rescues the (0,0) finite-geometry MATCH on the
        4 criteria; the N7 algebra-side rescue is what carries the recovery, N3 is untouched).
        Hence PERMANENT.

    Step 5 (Conclusion):
      The registry entry MUST be tagged CONTROLLED-RECOVERY (CONDITIONAL), with the N3 +
      KO-mismatch carried as PERMANENT obstructions. The two JOINT clauses the Stage-2
      reviewers PASS-AND are exactly: (C) "the recovery is controlled, residual ≤ 0.320
      KK-budget, NOT an isomorphism" and (D) "N3 + product-vs-finite KO-mismatch are
      PERMANENT, independent of the low-energy quotient." A reviewer who affirms an
      UNCONDITIONAL equivalence FAILS the gate (over-claims past the substitution chain).
      [SIGN] note: the directional content is the INEQUALITY KO_dim_product = 4 < KO_dim_fiber
      = 6 (the product UNDER-supplies the required KO-dim) and the residual sign
      0 < recovery_residual_KK_suppression_budget = 0.320 ≤ RECOVERY_FLOOR — both are
      affirmed-PERMANENT directions, not value-matches.

# ---- Verdict rubric ----
PASS_meaning: >
  STAGE-3-PERMANENT. The §VII.BH STAGE-1-CANDIDATE landed with all required fields, AND
  both cross-axis reviewers (NCG-axiomatic + substrate/superfluid), operating WITHOUT the
  W8-4 transcript, independently PASS all their single-axis clauses AND PASS-AND the two
  JOINT clauses (C controlled-recovery-not-isomorphism; D N3+KO-mismatch PERMANENT). The
  controlled-recovery theorem joins the permanent-results table; orchestrator flips the
  §VII.BH tag STAGE-1-CANDIDATE → STAGE-3-PERMANENT at session-end synthesis. Solution-space:
  the D_K≅D_F recovery is a structurally-confirmed CONDITIONAL bridge from the SU(3) fiber
  to the SM finite geometry — citable as a structural anchor with the obstruction-scope intact.
FAIL_meaning: >
  Holds at STAGE-1-CANDIDATE. At least one cross-reviewer returned FAIL on a clause (a
  single-axis clause OR a JOINT clause). The FAILing clause(s) route to next-session
  remediation; the §VII.BH entry remains a registered CANDIDATE (citable only with the
  STAGE-1-CANDIDATE qualifier). Solution-space: the controlled-recovery claim is registry-
  present but not yet structurally confirmed across axes — the disputed clause names the
  open question.
INFO_meaning: >
  Holds at STAGE-1-CANDIDATE with a Stage-2-INFO-deferred clause. A cross-reviewer returned
  INFO (not FAIL) on a clause — e.g. the 0.320 budget is affirmed as an O((E/M_KK)²) bound
  but the reviewer flags the const-mode projection choice as one-of-several admissible
  quotients (a PRU-adjacent diagnostic on the recovery map). The entry stays at Stage-1; the
  INFO clause is documented as Stage-2-INFO-deferred. ALSO the verdict-state if the registry
  landing succeeds but the Stage-2 reviewers cannot be dispatched in-session (mechanical
  closure on Component B per mechanical-closure-discipline.md, value='PRE-REG-INC_blocked_by_stage2_dispatch').

  Connes-Chamseddine SM finite geometry (A_F, H_F, D_F) up to the O((E/M_KK)²)=0.320
  KK-suppression budget. The direction of explanation flows FROM the substrate (the full
  D_K on SU(3)) TOWARD the emergent SM finite geometry (the low-energy const-mode block) —
  the SM finite triple is DERIVED as the IR limit of the fabric, never assumed. The
  obstructions are equally substrate-first: the product geometry M₄ × F under-supplies the
  KO-dim (4 < 6) the fiber demands, and the order-one axiom fails at norm 4.000 on the bare
  product — both are structural properties of the fabric, permanent under the low-energy
```

### §W5-1 Allowlist FLAG + classification (M1–M4)

**FLAG FOR ORCHESTRATOR**: the registry-landing component of `S97-DK-DF-STAGE2` is METHODOLOGY-class (artifact-existence + content on the §VII.BH registry entry, no numerical threshold on the landing itself). Per `.claude/rules/wave-classification.md §M4` + `.claude/rules/methodology-wave-allowlist.md`, the gate-ID `S97-DK-DF-STAGE2` must appear in the allowlist ledger (`sessions/framework/registry/methodology-wave-allowlist-ledger.md`) to satisfy M4.
```yaml
# ---- Identity (6 fields) ----
gate_id: "S97-Q10-1-PS-CONDENSATE"
schema_version: "R3"
trigger: "[VERIFY]"
classification: "GEOMETRIC"

  On the Pati–Salam extended finite triple A_K^{PS} = ℂ ⊕ M₂(ℂ)_L ⊕ M₂(ℂ)_R ⊕ M₄(ℂ),
  the kernel ker(ι_*^{PS}) of the inheritance morphism to the BdG/condensate sector either
  (PASS) forbids any non-abelian M₄(ℂ) symmetry-breaking condensate channel — i.e. the
  A_K abelian-only / color-singlet-forced theorem (D-2) EXTENDS to the rank-4 PS algebra —
  or (FAIL) admits a genuine non-abelian condensate class in M₄(ℂ), which would scope the
  W3 abelian-only result to A_K-specific.

method:
  description: >
    Build A_K^{PS} = ℂ ⊕ M₂(ℂ)_L ⊕ M₂(ℂ)_R ⊕ M₄(ℂ) (Artin–Wedderburn finite Type-I,
    4 simple summands). Construct the inheritance morphism ι^{PS} to the condensate sector
    analogous to the A_K case χ : ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ) → M₂(ℂ) (which sends M₃(ℂ) → 0, ker = M₃(ℂ)).
    For PS, the BdG/condensate map D_BdG = [[D_K, Δ],[Δ†, −D_K]] (S35) acts on the doubled
    Hilbert space; the condensate Δ transforms in a representation of A_K^{PS}. Compute
    ker(ι_*^{PS}) on cohomology. Then test, per summand of A_K^{PS}, whether a symmetry-
    breaking condensate channel is ABELIAN-FORCED (the order parameter must be a scalar /
    central element, color-singlet) or admits a NON-ABELIAN channel (the order parameter can
    carry a non-trivial M₄(ℂ) representation). Apply the A_K template's decision machinery:
    triality t = (p−q) mod 3 (the SU(3) color-grading that forced V(q⁺,q⁻)=0 on A_K), the
    Peter-Weyl block-diagonality of the relevant Dirac operator, and the S58 order-one-
    failure-at-norm-4 repair route (which is what motivates the PS extension). PASS iff the
    M₄(ℂ) condensate is color-singlet-forced (abelian-only EXTENDS); FAIL iff a non-abelian
    M₄(ℂ) channel exists; INFO iff the extended morphism admits non-unique repair routes
    (PRU on the morphism — multiple inequivalent ι^{PS} give different kernels).
  producing_script: "computations/_shared/s97_q10_1_ps_condensate.py"

# ---- PRDR Checklist (8 items) ----

# (1) operator — set-membership / channel-admissibility classification
operator:
  type: "set"
  form: >
    PASS  ⟺  ∀ symmetry-breaking condensate channel c on A_K^{PS}:
                c is color-singlet-forced (order parameter ∈ center / scalar block), i.e.
                the M₄(ℂ) summand admits NO non-abelian condensate (abelian-only EXTENDS).
    FAIL  ⟺  ∃ a condensate channel c whose order parameter carries a non-trivial M₄(ℂ)
                irrep (a non-abelian class in ker(ι_*^{PS})).
    INFO  ⟺  the extended inheritance morphism ι^{PS} is non-unique (≥2 inequivalent repair
                routes give different ker(ι_*^{PS})) ⇒ PRU on the extended morphism.

# (2) strict_PASS_boundary — set-membership classification, not a scalar threshold
strict_PASS_boundary:
  value: "N/A — channel-admissibility set-membership (abelian-only EXTENDS vs non-abelian class admitted); criterion in operator.form + verdict rubric"
  direction: "="

# (3) boundary_reachable_analytically
boundary_reachable_analytically:
  bool: true
  proof_ref: "the A_K template is analytic (ker(χ)=M₃(ℂ), V(q⁺,q⁻)=0 by triality, S88 W3a); the PS extension applies the same representation-theoretic machinery to the rank-4 algebra — the classification is a finite representation-theory computation, exact"

# (4) reachable_rationals
reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: true
  mesh_density: "discrete — the admissible condensate channels are a finite set indexed by the irreps of A_K^{PS} summands (dims {1, 2_L, 2_R, 4}); the classification is over this finite index set"

# (5) machinery_pin_map
machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "finite — enumerate condensate channels over the 4 simple summands {ℂ, M₂(ℂ)_L, M₂(ℂ)_R, M₄(ℂ)} and their irreps"
  L_max: 10                                   # Peter-Weyl block-diag truncation for the orbital sector (D_K block-diag pre-check applies, see below)
  scan_range: "N/A — finite representation-theory enumeration, no continuous scan"
  step_size: "N/A — discrete summand/irrep enumeration"
  tolerance: 1.0e-12                           # exact (rational / integer) classification; tolerance only for the numerical Peter-Weyl block-diag cross-check
  scheme: "PATI-SALAM-RANK4-INHERITANCE-KERNEL"
  convention: "ABELIAN-ONLY-EXTENSION-TEST (color-singlet-forced vs non-abelian-class-admitted)"
  random_seed: "N/A — deterministic"
  GPU_path: "torch.linalg"                     # the PS-sector D_BdG eigenproblem at L_max=10 is block-diagonal by Peter-Weyl; largest block well within VRAM (see D_K block-diag pre-check)
  # Casimir-bound pre-check (D_K block-diag, math-scripts.md §"D_K Block-Diagonality"):
  Dk_block_diag_precheck: >
    D_K (and the PS-extended orbital Dirac) is BLOCK-DIAGONAL by Peter-Weyl: D_K = ⊕_{(p,q)} D_{(p,q)}.
    At L_max=10 the largest single block is well within the 17.1 GB VRAM cap (dense storage of the
    bottom-block ≪ 0.5×VRAM). Sparse storage is NOT necessary. The operative cost is irrep
    CONSTRUCTION (recursive Casimir projection), feasible at p+q ≤ 10 within an agent timeslot.
    The condensate classification only needs the SUMMAND-irrep structure of A_K^{PS}, which is
    finite-dimensional (dims {1,2,2,4}) and does NOT require the full orbital tower — the orbital
    Peter-Weyl sector enters only as the V(q⁺,q⁻)=0 triality cross-check.
  ker_template: "ker(χ_{A_K}) = M₃(ℂ); triality t=(p−q) mod 3; V(q⁺,q⁻)=0 (S88 W3a A_K template)"
  bdg_map: "D_BdG = [[D_K, Δ],[Δ†, −D_K]] (S35); Δ = condensate order parameter, transforms in a rep of A_K^{PS}"
  ps_repair_route: "S58 order-one-failure-at-norm-4.000 → Pati-Salam extension (SU(4) ⊃ SU(3)×U(1))"

# (6) audit_discriminators
audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap", "A_K^PS-algebra-spec", "A_K-ker-template"]
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

# (7) substitution_chain — the warrant for the abelian-only EXTENSION direction
substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "On A_K^{PS}, whether the M₄(ℂ) summand admits a non-abelian condensate is decided
            by whether the inheritance kernel ker(ι_*^{PS}) intersected with M₄(ℂ) contains a
            non-central (non-scalar) class; on A_K the analog kernel ker(χ)=M₃(ℂ) was
            color-singlet-FORCED by triality V(q⁺,q⁻)=0, so the question is whether the same
            triality-forcing EXTENDS to the rank-4 algebra."

    Step 1 (Definitions):
      A_K        = ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ)                              [the SM finite algebra]
      A_K^{PS}   = ℂ ⊕ M₂(ℂ)_L ⊕ M₂(ℂ)_R ⊕ M₄(ℂ)             [Pati-Salam extension, S58 repair]
      χ          : A_K → M₂(ℂ),  M₃(ℂ) → 0,  ker(χ) = M₃(ℂ)   [A_K inheritance morphism, S88 W3a]
      ι^{PS}     : A_K^{PS} → (condensate/BdG sector)          [PS inheritance morphism, to construct]
      D_BdG      = [[D_K, Δ],[Δ†, −D_K]]                       [S35; Δ = order parameter]
      triality   t(p,q) = (p−q) mod 3                          [SU(3) color-grading]
      V(q⁺,q⁻)   = 0  on A_K                                   [color-singlet forcing: the off-diagonal
                                                                condensate vertex vanishes by triality]

    Step 2 (Substitute — the A_K result):
      On A_K, a symmetry-breaking condensate channel c has order parameter Δ_c ∈ a rep of A_K.
      The triality grading forces the off-diagonal vertex V(q⁺,q⁻) = 0 ⇒ Δ_c must be color-singlet
      (Δ_c ∈ ℂ ⊕ ℍ, NOT in M₃(ℂ) as a non-central element) ⇒ abelian-only / color-singlet-forced.
      (D-2 theorem: the M₃(ℂ) condensate is forbidden; the order parameter is central.)

    Step 3 (Simplify — what changes for PS):
      A_K^{PS} replaces { ℍ → M₂(ℂ)_L ⊕ M₂(ℂ)_R } (left-right symmetric) and { M₃(ℂ) → M₄(ℂ) }
      (color SU(3) → Pati-Salam SU(4), lepton = 4th color). The question reduces to:
        does the M₄(ℂ) summand carry a triality-like grading that forces its condensate vertex
        to vanish (V^{PS} = 0), OR does the SU(4) structure ADMIT a non-abelian condensate
        (e.g. a (15) adjoint or (6)/(10) order parameter breaking SU(4) → SU(3)×U(1))?
      The decision is: compute ker(ι_*^{PS}) ∩ M₄(ℂ) and test for a non-central class.

    Step 4 (Direction):
      IF the M₄(ℂ) condensate vertex vanishes by an SU(4)-grading analog of triality
         ⇒ ker(ι_*^{PS}) ∩ M₄(ℂ) contains only central (scalar) classes
         ⇒ abelian-only EXTENDS  ⇒  PASS  (D-2 generalizes; the color-singlet-forcing is
            algebra-independent within the AF-Wedderburn class).
      IF instead SU(4) admits a non-abelian breaking channel (the (15) adjoint condensate is the
         canonical Pati-Salam SU(4)→SU(3)×U(1) breaking)
         ⇒ ker(ι_*^{PS}) ∩ M₄(ℂ) contains a non-central class
         ⇒ FAIL  (W3 is A_K-specific; the abelian-only theorem does NOT extend; this is a
            SCOPE-REFINEMENT of D-2, NOT a Q10 reopening — Q10 stays closed, the scope narrows).
      [NOTE — pre-registration honesty]: the physically-expected Pati-Salam breaking
      SU(4) → SU(3)_c × U(1)_{B−L} is driven by a (15)-adjoint condensate, which IS non-abelian.
      The gate is GENUINELY OPEN between PASS and FAIL because the inheritance-kernel question
      (does ι_*^{PS} ANNIHILATE that (15) channel, as χ annihilated M₃(ℂ)?) is distinct from the
      bare group-theory of SU(4) breaking. The verdict is NOT pre-judged.

    Step 5 (Conclusion):
      PASS = abelian-only EXTENDS (M₄(ℂ) condensate color-singlet-forced via an SU(4)-triality
             analog) ⇒ D-2 generalizes, W3 is algebra-independent.
      FAIL = M₄(ℂ) admits a non-abelian class (e.g. (15)-adjoint in ker(ι_*^{PS})) ⇒ W3 scope
             narrows to A_K-specific (scope-refinement, Q10 stays closed).
      INFO = ι^{PS} non-unique (PRU on the extended morphism) ⇒ the repair route is not pinned.
```

## §W5-3. S97-DS-AREA-LAW-MONOTONICITY

```yaml

gate_id: "S97-DS-AREA-LAW-MONOTONICITY"
schema_version: "R3"
trigger: "[SIGN]"

  Casimir-Monotonicity ratio — or (FAIL/INFO) inherits the S63 black-hole derivation ONLY

    monotonicity) Construct a candidate cosmological-horizon entropy functional M_dS(τ) from
    substrate spectral monotonicity: the de Sitter horizon radius R_H = √(3/Λ) with Λ set by

    a₀ → Λ → R_H = √(3/Λ)); the horizon AREA A = 4π R_H²; the entropy from the substrate
    monotone (the cosmological analog of the S63 chain
    substrate-spectral-monotonicity → BCS-coherence-suppression → vacuum-energy-reduction →
    area-theorem, but with the dS horizon replacing the BH horizon). (CROSS-CHECK,
    Gibbons-Hawking) the standard S_dS = 3π/(Λℓ_P²) = A/4G. Then TEST whether M_dS(τ) is
    ALGEBRAICALLY INDEPENDENT of the a₀/a₂-inherited route: via Sage-MCP sage_simplify, form
    the difference [M_dS(τ)] − [S63-BH-chain ∘ radius-map] and test whether it vanishes
    IDENTICALLY (⇒ INFO, algebraically equivalent, not independent) or whether M_dS(τ) carries
    monotonicity content NOT reducible to the a₀/a₂ ratio (⇒ PASS, independent). The S65
    EIH Casimir-Monotonicity theorem (local a₀/a₂ ↑ with C₂(p,q), PERMANENT) is the
    ratio-lock the PASS route must NOT consume.
  producing_script: "computations/_shared/s97_ds_area_law_monotonicity.py"

# ---- PRDR Checklist (8 items) ----

  type: "set"

    PASS  ⟺  ∃ M_dS(τ) (a substrate-spectral-monotonicity functional) such that
                M_dS reproduces S_dS = A/4G  ∧  M_dS does NOT consume the S65 a₀/a₂ ratio
                (i.e. d M_dS / d(a₀/a₂) is NOT the sole monotonicity source —

                |Δ| < 1e-12) — algebraically EQUIVALENT, exact but NOT independent.
    FAIL  ⟺  no functional distinct from the a₀/a₂-inherited one reproduces S_dS = A/4G
                (the dS area law inherits the BH derivation ONLY through the ratio lock).

# (2) strict_PASS_boundary — the INFO sub-criterion carries the only scalar tolerance

# (4) reachable_rationals
reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: false
  mesh_density: "continuous — τ ∈ [τ_fold, 0.6] grid for the M_dS(τ) monotonicity check; the equivalence test itself is symbolic (no mesh)"

# (5) machinery_pin_map
machinery_pin_map:

  L_max: 10                                    # Peter-Weyl truncation for the a₀, a₂ spectral moments (consistent with a0_fold/a2_fold provenance)
  scan_range: "[0.190, 0.6]"                   # τ from τ_fold to late-time (matches the S97 W1 a(t) window)
```

```yaml
  trace-preserving), rather than changing type (e.g. a II_1 trace-collapse).

  description: >

    Peter-Weyl inclusion system: A_K^{≤L} ↪ A_K^{≤L+1} via the block-diagonal inclusion adding
    the new (p,q) sectors with p+q = L+1 (the connecting maps of the AF tower). (2) Compute the

    Artin-Wedderburn, n_Wedderburn_factors = 3, AF block dims [1,1,9] per s96 npz). (3) Classify
    the LIMIT: the decisive criterion is the trace-range of the inductive-limit trace. For an AF
    algebra A = lim A_n with connecting maps φ_n: A_n → A_{n+1}, the limit is Type-I_∞
    (hyperfinite) iff the trace takes DISCRETE values (the dimension function ranges over a
    discrete subgroup, no trace-collapse to a continuum), and is II_1 iff the normalized trace
    ranges CONTINUOUSLY over [0,1] (the Glimm UHF / Bratteli-diagram criterion). Compute the
    Bratteli diagram of the canonical Peter-Weyl tower (the multiplicity matrix of the

    INFO = the type depends on the inclusion choice (the canonical Peter-Weyl tower selects one,
    but a different inclusion system would give a different type).

  wedderburn: "A_K = ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ); n_Wedderburn_factors = 3; AF block dims [1,1,9] (s96 npz AF_block_dims_complex)"
  dim_formula: "dim V_{(p,q)} = ½(p+1)(q+1)(p+q+2) (SU(3) Weyl dimension; the multiplicity-matrix entries)"

# (6) audit_discriminators
audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap", "ds1-ref", "canonical-inclusion-spec"]
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

# (7) substitution_chain — MANDATORY ([VERIFY-THEOREM]: the discrete-vs-continuous trace direction)
substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "The AF inductive limit lim_{L→∞} A_K^{≤L} STAYS Type-I (hyperfinite Type-I_∞) iff
            its inductive-limit trace is DISCRETE; it would be II_1 iff the normalized trace
            ranges continuously over [0,1]. The canonical Peter-Weyl tower has integer
            multiplicity matrices with a discrete dimension group, so the limit is Type-I_∞."

    Step 1 (Definitions, cited):
      A_K^{≤L}    = bicommutant of A_K on H_K^{≤L} = ⊕_{(p,q)}^{≤L} V_{(p,q)} ⊗ ℂ¹⁶
                    [finite Type-I per stage, DS.1; Artin-Wedderburn n_factors = 3]
      φ_L         : A_K^{≤L} ↪ A_K^{≤L+1}     [canonical Peter-Weyl inclusion, adds p+q=L+1 shells]
      dim V_{(p,q)} = ½(p+1)(q+1)(p+q+2)       [SU(3) Weyl dimension; integer multiplicity entries]
      K₀(A)       = dimension group of A = lim A_n  [Bratteli-Elliott invariant]
      trace-range = the set of values the (normalized) trace takes on projections

    Step 2 (Substitute — the AF type criterion, Bratteli-Elliott):
      For an AF algebra A = lim (A_n, φ_n):
        A is Type-I_∞ (hyperfinite)  ⟺  K₀(A) is a discrete ordered group (trace DISCRETE);
        A is II_1 (hyperfinite II_1) ⟺  the normalized trace ranges over a DENSE subset of [0,1]
                                          (UHF-type collapse, e.g. the CAR algebra ⊗ M_2(ℂ)).
      Each A_K^{≤L} = ⊕ matrix blocks with INTEGER dims (dim V_{(p,q)} · 16 per sector).
      The inclusion φ_L adds new integer-dim blocks; the multiplicity matrix entries are integers.

    Step 3 (Simplify — the dimension group of the Peter-Weyl tower):
      The Bratteli diagram of A_K^{≤L} ↪ A_K^{≤L+1} is a sequence of integer multiplicity
      matrices. The dimension group K₀ = lim (ℤ^{r_L}, M_L) where r_L = number of simple summands
      at stage L and M_L the integer multiplicity matrix. Because the connecting maps are
      block-diagonal inclusions (each old block embeds with multiplicity 1 into the corresponding
      new block, plus genuinely NEW blocks for the new shells), the trace of a projection in any
      A_K^{≤L} is a sum of integer-weighted block-traces — it does NOT densify into [0,1].

    Step 4 (Direction — discrete trace ⇒ Type-I_∞):
      The trace-range is the set { Σ_i n_i d_i : n_i ∈ ℤ≥0, d_i = block dims } — a DISCRETE
      additive subset (the block dims are integers; the trace lands on a lattice, not a continuum).
      ⇒ K₀ is discrete  ⇒  the limit is hyperfinite Type-I_∞  ⇒  PASS (stays Type-I).

      direct-sum extension. Hence DISCRETE, hence Type-I_∞.
      [VERIFY-THEOREM] directional content: the trace-range is DISCRETE (the affirmed direction),
      NOT continuous-over-[0,1].

    Step 5 (Conclusion):
      PASS = stays Type-I: the canonical Peter-Weyl inductive limit is hyperfinite Type-I_∞

      FAIL = non-Type-I AF limit (continuous [0,1] trace ⇒ II_1) — would require a densifying
             (UHF-tensor-product) inclusion the Peter-Weyl tower does NOT have.
      INFO = the type depends on the inclusion choice: the canonical Peter-Weyl tower (the one
             DS.1 + S22b block-diag select) gives Type-I_∞, but an ALTERNATIVE inclusion system
             (e.g. a tensor-product / UHF re-embedding) would give II_1 — so the type is
             tower-dependent, and the canonical choice must be declared.

# ---- Verdict rubric ----
PASS_meaning: >
  The inductive limit STAYS Type-I: lim_{L→∞} (A_K^{≤L}, H_K^{≤L}, D_K^{≤L}) is a hyperfinite
  AF Type-I_∞ von Neumann algebra. The canonical Peter-Weyl connecting maps are trace-preserving;
  the dimension group K₀ is discrete; no II_1 collapse. Solution-space: the substrate algebra's
  L_max→∞ completion is Type-I_∞ — a well-defined trace exists, the fabric's operator algebra is
  the expected hyperfinite Type-I limit, and DS.1's per-stage finiteness lifts to the tower.
FAIL_meaning: >
  Non-Type-I AF limit: the normalized inductive-limit trace ranges continuously over [0,1]
  (II_1 trace-collapse). The L_max→∞ completion is a hyperfinite II_1 factor, NOT Type-I — the
  type CHANGES in the limit even though each finite stage is Type-I. Solution-space: the tower
  densifies into a II_1 factor (a structurally significant change — the substrate algebra is a
  factor of continuous dimension, with implications for the trace / Dixmier-trace structure).
INFO_meaning: >
  The type DEPENDS on the inclusion choice. The canonical Peter-Weyl tower (DS.1 + S22b
  block-diag) selects Type-I_∞, but an ALTERNATIVE inclusion system (e.g. a UHF tensor-product
  re-embedding) would give II_1. Solution-space: the von Neumann type is not an intrinsic
  invariant of the abstract sequence but of the chosen inductive system; the canonical
  Peter-Weyl inclusion must be declared to fix the type (and it gives Type-I_∞).

# ---- Effort + framing ----
effort:
  files_created:
    - "computations/session-97/s97_vn_type_inductive_limit.py"
    - "computations/session-97/s97_vn_type_inductive_limit.npz"
    - "computations/session-97/s97_vn_type_inductive_limit.png"
  estimated_time: "medium (Bratteli-diagram / dimension-group classification from the closed-form Peter-Weyl dims)"

substrate_framing: |
  GEOMETRIC. The substrate fabric at every point is the spectral triple on SU(3); the operator
  algebra A_K = ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ) acts block-diagonally (Peter-Weyl) on H_K = ⊕_{(p,q)} V_{(p,q)} ⊗
  ℂ¹⁶. Each finite-L_max truncation is a finite Type-I von Neumann algebra (DS.1) — the fabric
  truncated to its bottom (p,q) shells is a finite direct sum of matrix algebras. The question is
  what the FULL fabric (L_max → ∞) is, as a von Neumann algebra: the inductive limit of the
  truncations. The Murray–von Neumann type is the decisive operator-algebraic invariant: Type-I_∞
  (a well-defined trace, the expected hyperfinite AF limit) vs II_1 (a continuous-dimension factor,
  a trace-collapse). This is a property of the FABRIC ITSELF (the substrate algebra), classified
  from its Bratteli diagram — the integer multiplicity matrices of the Peter-Weyl inclusion tower.
  The direction is substrate-first: the type is DERIVED from the substrate's own spectral
  decomposition (the closed-form SU(3) Weyl dimensions ½(p+1)(q+1)(p+q+2)), never imposed. A
  Type-I_∞ result certifies that the fabric's operator algebra admits the traces (operator trace,
  Dixmier trace, zeta-regularization) the spectral-action and index-theory machinery require.
```
